title: Aggrega Infrastructure Base (Recipe)
description: Ops-authored pointer and mapping layer connecting Dev intent to a specific infrastructure execution engine. Strictly 1:1 with a physical provider and catalog component.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the implementation recipe (e.g., 2.1.0).

description.description: A concise, one-sentence summary of what the entity does.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers who own this entity.

repository.description: The URL to the Git repository where the source files live.

home.description: The URL of this entity's home page, wiki, or documentation.

keywords.description: A list of descriptive keywords for UI discoverability.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this entity is deprecated and should no longer be used.

spec.description: The provider binding, source, value mapping, and pipeline for a Recipe. Supports three input kinds composed by addition: sourced (source plus valuesMapping overlay), synthesized (workload), and artifacts (named output files).

then.description: The eval provider executes formatting in-memory. Fetching a 'source', a 'workload', 'artifacts', or utilizing base mapping fields is mathematically banned.

else.description: Non-eval providers use the three-input-kinds model. At least one input kind must be present: sourced (source + values overlay), synthesized (workload), or artifacts. Pairing rules apply: valuesMapping pairs with source; and a workload: block requires a provider whose engine supports workload synthesis — a synthesized-mode Recipe bound to a non-synthesizing provider halts loudly at render time.

provider.description: The explicit execution engine this recipe targets (e.g., 'helm', 'terraform', 'compose', 'eval').

implements.description: Declares which catalog component type this recipe is able to implement (exact version 'core/api-server:1.0.0', major-compatible range 'core/api-server:^1.0.0', or unversioned 'core/api-server'). The compiler uses it to verify Manifest mappings and to suggest candidates in diagnostics and editor completion; it never resolves a build. The Manifest mapping is the user's explicit deployment choice, pinned in the lockfile.

source.description: The location of the infrastructure code. Accepts a Universal URI string, or an open structured object whose provider-defined keys are exposed to the Recipe's templates as '.source.*'.

oneOf.description: Universal URI string (e.g., './src', 'git::https://...', 'oci://...'). Used for local paths, OCI artifacts, and Git repositories.

Open Structured Object (additionalProperties: true). Its keys are provider-defined and are exposed to the Recipe's templates as '.source.*' (for example '.source.chart'). By design the core is schema-agnostic: each provider's WebAssembly socket is intended to define and validate its own source shape (such as 'registry'/'chart' for Helm, or 'workspace' for Terraform). CURRENT SHIPPED BEHAVIOR: per-provider Wasm source validation is not yet implemented. The core resolves a FETCHED source by the { kind, url, version } form, where 'kind' selects a built-in resolver (today: helm-oci-chart, helm-https-chart, compose-https-fragment). A fetch-intended source must therefore use { kind, url, version }; a structured source without 'kind'/'url' is not fetched, and if a fetch was intended it fails loudly at lock-time source descent rather than silently resolving to nothing. When the per-provider Wasm socket ships it will validate provider-specific shapes and translate them ahead-of-time into a deterministic { kind, url, version } fetch identity.

locals.description: The Private Ops State. Internal computation results available only within this Recipe's templates (valuesMapping, provides, pipeline[].with). Used to export physical realities (e.g., target containers, JSON paths) for downstream Wasm plugins. Never exposed to callers — use provides for the public API.

provides.description: The Public Developer API. Contractual output variables available for downstream Caller inject resolution. The compiler evaluates provides templates in Pass 1 (self-contained, any order). Callers resolve inject keys against these values in Pass 2. Values are scalars — the pipe carries them blindly and stringifies deterministically at the injection boundary.

valuesMapping.description: Values mapping content with three authoring modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar (typically block-scalar YAML `|`) producing the provider's expected values format from Aggrega context (.values, .secrets, .infra). Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.tmpl`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Mode 3 (library import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: <Library>#/mappings/<entry>`, referencing a MappingLibrary entry by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference).

workload.description: Workload YAML producer with two authoring modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar whose output parses as 'aggrega.ai/v1alpha1 Workload'. Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.yaml`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Library imports are not supported at this site — use a local file path. The target Provider's engine must support workload synthesis; the standard-library catalog declares workloadSchema on such providers as the documented contract. A workload: Recipe bound to a provider whose engine cannot synthesize halts loudly at render time.

$import.description: Local file path. Library imports are not supported at workload: — use a local file path.

artifacts.description: Map of output filename to artifact-content authoring. Each entry's value carries one of two modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar whose output is the artifact body. Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.yaml`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Library imports are not supported at this site — use a local file path. Map keys become output filenames verbatim. Collisions across artifact entries, source output, workload synthesis are load-time or render-time errors.

$import.description: Local file path. Library imports are not supported at artifacts:.

pipeline.description: Sequential list of Wasm plugins to execute for stateful AST mutation directly on the base infrastructure.

id.description: A unique programmatic identifier for this step, allowing downstream plugins to reference its outputs.

plugin.description: The Universal URI of the executable Go plugin.

function.description: The exported Wasm function to invoke.

with.description: Inline Go template evaluating to a JSON/YAML map that strictly satisfies this plugin's explicit input schema.

optional.description: When true, a failure of this step (a guest trap, a patch targeting a document not present in the set, a malformed patch, or an error-severity diagnostic) is downgraded to a loud warning: the pre-step document set is restored, this step's output is discarded, and the pipeline continues. When false or absent, any step failure halts the build after restoring the pre-step document set.

assertions.description: Build-time cross-field validation. Each entry is a named assertion: the key is a stable rule identifier surfaced in error messages; the value is a Go template string with `{{ fail "message" }}` halt semantics. Multiple named assertions per entity evaluate per-instance in author-declared order; the first failing assertion halts the build. Recipe assertions evaluate at Step 5b (post-binding, post-allProvides-evaluation, pre-render) and express implementation invariants of the specific wrapped chart or module. Template context: .values / .infra / .uses / .secrets / .metadata plus .provides / .locals / .recipe. The evaluator uses missingkey=error: references to undefined keys halt with a no-such-key diagnostic; optional-field idioms use Sprig default / hasKey.
